items.title: HCI One consolidates eight paramedical labels on the FysioRoadmap web foundation, discipline by discipline and without a forced migration deadline
items.summary: HCI One is presented as a new multidisciplinary paramedical platform built on the web-based FysioRoadmap foundation that brings FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura, Evry, Abakus, Podofile, Edevop and FysioLogic together in one environment for administration, documentation, planning and communication. The rollout is phased per discipline, physiotherapy first; existing users keep full support on their current label and choose their own transition moment, with no forced migration deadline. Vortex describes HCI as a 2021 buyout with founder Eric de Boer followed by a buy-and-build programme of more than 14 add-on acquisitions, and the May 2025 CEO announcement states that Robin Dunki Jacobs — who joined in 2024 as Business Unit Director responsible for integrating the labels — will integrate the acquired solutions, expand digital patient access through a unified network and invest in digital triage, AI and e-health.
items.implication: Label consolidation is the domain's multi-year operating risk, not a one-off project: every acquired label keeps a loyal user base that must be migrated voluntarily, so the migration tooling, per-discipline readiness and hypercare capacity of the implementation team decide how fast HCI One absorbs the installed base, while the CEO mandate ties the paramedical platform to the patient front door and triage roadmap.

items.title: From 7,500 professionals and €500 million in declarations in 2022 to 40,000 professionals and 4 million users: scale is HCI's proposition to practices and partners alike
items.summary: At the June 2022 investment announcement HCI served more than 7,500 professionals, processed more than €500 million in annual declarations, had a team of 45+ and reached 2 million+ patients, with the stated ambition of relieving the administrative burden of 20,000 professionals; the 2021 buyout was made with founder Eric de Boer, who previously founded Incura and Winbase. The August 2024 press release on SpotOnMedics (founded 2011 in Hoofddorp, acquired from VvAA, director Geert van den Enden) called HCI the market leader in physiotherapy software, supporting 1 in 4 paramedics. The home page now states 4 million+ patients and 40,000+ healthcare professionals every day, NEN 7510 and ISO 27001 certification, and a partner list including DigiDoc, HC, QUIN, ProMedico, Pharmapartners, MicroHIS, Fysio AI, PhysioTrack and Vecozo.
items.implication: The declaration volume flowing through the platform makes first-time acceptance and Vecozo throughput a revenue-critical KPI for practices and for HCI's billing services, and the installed base is the asset that integration partners pay attention to — so the partner API, onboarding capacity and declaration engine should be sized for a group five times larger than the one Vortex bought.

items.title: Vecozo retired PM304: treatments from 1 January 2025 must be declared in GDS801, so every paramedical EPD carries two declaration standards side by side
items.summary: The LVVP newsletter reports that Vecozo has taken the old paramedical declaration standard out of service: treatments with a treatment date from 1 January 2025 must be declared with GDS801, while PM304 remains in use only for treatment dates up to and including 31 December 2024. The GDS-PM standard was developed jointly by PPN, KNGF, ZN, Vektis, Vecozo and the EPD vendors.
items.implication: Standard switches are dated by treatment date, not by submission date, so the declaration engine must route each claim to the right standard from the episode's dates and keep PM304 corrections working for the tail of 2024 episodes; because vendors co-develop the standard, HCI's declaration team should be in the working group early enough to ship before the cut-over and to brief the implementation desk on the return-message patterns that follow it.

items.title: The 2026 zorgprestatiemodel field agreements add a mandatory referral date to every GGZ declaration and end the transitional benefit — changes that land in the EPD, not in the consulting room
items.summary: According to the LVVP, the 2026 field agreements for the zorgprestatiemodel require a referral date on every declaration so that waiting times can be tracked, add the system therapist to the professional standards, and permanently discontinue the transitional benefit, while the core model of consults, settings and professionals is unchanged.
items.implication: Registration compliance for GGZ is a yearly release train driven by field agreements: the registration module must make the referral date a required, validated field at intake, extend the professional list, and remove retired tariff logic before 1 January, and the implementation team needs a pre-year-end change-communication and configuration routine for institutions and independent practitioners alike.

items.title: GGZ waiting times exceed the Treeknorm in every region, and CRS's client portal with self-scheduling and secure contact is where intake friction can be taken out
items.summary: The LVVP summary of the Regiomonitor for the first half of 2025 states that GGZ waiting times exceed the 14-week Treeknorm in all regions, with only basic GGZ exactly at the norm. HCI describes CRS as an all-in-one EPD for GGZ and youth care with dossiers, treatment plans, medication, agenda and declarations, a central client portal, SmartAI voice-to-text and reporting, with integrations to Embloom, Bergop, Therapieland, ZorgDomein, ZorgMail and Minddistrict.
items.implication: Waiting-list management and intake are the GGZ practitioner's most visible pain, so portal self-scheduling, secure messaging and intake questionnaires should be measured as time-to-first-contact and no-show reduction rather than as portal features, and CRS reporting should expose waiting-time data in the form regional collaborations and the referral-date rule now demand.

items.title: The top-50 GGZ EPD market is held by five vendors and two portals; Quli reaches 4 percent of it while Wegiz pushes institutions toward PGO connections
items.summary: M&I/Partners' 2025 inventory of the 50 largest GGZ organisations by revenue counts SDB Groep at 15 organisations (30%), Nedap at 14 (27%), PinkRoccade at 7 (14%), Adapcare at 6 (12%) and Nexus at 5 (10%), notes that GGZ Friesland switched to Nedap, and lists client portals Caren and Karify at 22.5% each with Quli at 4% (two organisations). MedMij's FAQ for care providers explains that digital data exchange has been mandated by Wegiz since April 2023, that about 50% of GGZ institutions are connected to PGOs, that 16 MedMij-labelled PGOs existed in November 2025, and that paramedical care is still in an exploratory phase for PGO disclosure.
items.implication: For large institutions HCI competes as a portal and PGO layer on top of other vendors' EPDs at least as often as with CRS itself, so Quli's MedMij data exchange must work against SDB, Nedap and PinkRoccade records; for paramedical practices and GP partners the PGO obligation is still ahead, which makes Uw Zorg Online's MedMij position an early-mover asset rather than a compliance cost.

items.title: Uw Zorg Online is the digital front door for GP practices and pharmacies — 3 million+ app users booking, asking and ordering directly into the practice systems
items.summary: HCI presents Uw Zorg Online as the digital front door with e-consult for care questions, records access, medication and repeat prescriptions, self-measurements, appointments booked directly in the practice agenda and triage ('Moet ik naar de Dokter?'). It connects to the practice information systems Sanday, HealthConnected, Pharmapartners, CGM, Bricks and Vertimart, is MedMij-certified, reports 3 million+ app users after 20+ years, and merged into HCI in June 2023. The home page lists the partner ecosystem around it, including ProMedico, Pharmapartners and MicroHIS, and states that HCI serves 4 million+ patients.
items.implication: For the patient the app is one front door across GP, pharmacy and therapist, but for HCI it is a connector product whose value depends on HIS/AIS integrations that other vendors control: connector reliability, appointment-write-back and repeat-prescription completion are the metrics that decide whether a practice's phone traffic actually drops, and each HIS vendor is a partner relationship to be managed like a product.

items.title: Embloom brings 500+ questionnaires and 450 e-health interventions into the EPD, built over 15 years from the first Dutch digital triage tool
items.summary: HCI describes Embloom as 500+ questionnaires and 450 e-health interventions fully integrated in the EPD, supporting hybrid care for GGZ and somatic care. Vortex's July 2024 announcement states that Embloom was founded in 2010 in Maastricht, has 35 employees, 500+ questionnaires and 300+ treatment modules, serves 270,000+ users per year at about 2,500 organisations in the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany, and that HCI then had 35,000 providers and 3.5 million users. Embloom's own 15-year anniversary article traces the company from its founding as TelePsy in Maastricht by Marco Essed in 2010 to a complete e-health platform and the 2024 move under HCI, where it is also ISO 27001 and NEN 7510 certified.
items.implication: E-health content is a product line with its own roadmap (GGZ and somatic care, three countries) and its own users across roughly 2,500 organisations, many of which do not run CRS: keep Embloom integrable with third-party EPDs while making the CRS integration the deepest, and measure ROM completion and module usage per treatment rather than library size, because 'fully integrated' only pays off when questionnaires are sent, completed and read inside the dossier.

items.title: Administrative burden and low reimbursement rates are the sector's key problems for first-line physiotherapists (Nivel registered 7,848 of them in 543 practices in 2024), which is why voice-to-text and AI documentation are the platform's headline promise
items.summary: Nivel Zorgregistraties Eerste Lijn counted 7,848 physiotherapists in the 543 first-line practices that take part in its registration network, treating 1,162,545 patients in 2024; the network is a national sample, not the whole sector. The Fysiovakbond FDV report on employment conditions in first-line physiotherapy (2024) describes a sector with a high administrative burden and low reimbursement rates, in which physiotherapists spend about a full working day per week on administration. HCI's stated strategy under the new CEO is to integrate the acquired solutions and invest in digital triage, AI and e-health, CRS already includes SmartAI voice-to-text, and the group's mission is 'more time for care through more ease for providers and patients'.
items.implication: Administration minutes per treatment is the north-star metric the whole paramedical proposition must move, so voice-to-text, guideline templates and agenda-driven declarations should be evaluated on measured typing time and rework per episode; with reimbursement rates fixed by insurers, practices can only protect margin through time saved, which makes the case for HCI One and for premium documentation features concrete.

items.title: 24/7 online booking synced with the agenda, mobile agendas across locations, BI dashboards, Mollie payments and outsourced billing are the practice-operations feature set — at a price point third parties call the cheapest in the market
items.summary: The SpotOnMedics functions page lists 24/7 online booking synchronised with the agenda, a mobile agenda across locations, BI dashboards on production, revenue, treatment duration and referrers, specialisation cards, EU cloud hosting, Mollie payment integration, outsourced billing services that also handle return messages, and group management for lessons and subscriptions, with a custom quote within one business day. Incura offers a web-based dossier with customisable care pathways for physiotherapy, speech therapy, occupational therapy, exercise therapy and dietetics, an agenda and a management dashboard, and reports about 7,500 providers, 2 million+ patients and 20 years in the market. Physitrack's July 2026 comparison of Dutch physiotherapy EPDs calls SpotOnMedics FysioOne the cheapest option at about €5 per user per month and FysioRoadmap the strongest content-focused EPD (third-party claims).
items.implication: Practice owners buy an operating system for the agenda and cash flow, not a dossier: online booking share, invoice-to-payment time and dashboard usage are the adoption signals to track, billing services turn return-message handling into a paid HCI service with its own SLA, and the price spread between labels means HCI One must justify its positioning by measurable time saved rather than by feature parity.

items.title: Exercise apps, quality registers, payment, referral and HIS vendors connect to HCI labels one by one today — Physitrack alone maintains eleven Dutch EPD integrations
items.summary: Physitrack's 2026 comparison lists Dutch EPD systems including Intramed, Incura, Abakus, Fysiomanager, SpotOnMedics and James Software and states that Physitrack has eleven active Dutch EPD integrations; FysioRoadmap also names Physitrack among its partners. HCI's home page names DigiDoc, HC, QUIN, ProMedico, Pharmapartners, MicroHIS, Fysio AI, PhysioTrack and Vecozo as partners; Incura lists Physitrack, Mollie, Abakus, Vecozo, Kiwa, KNGF, Philips, MediQuest and QualiView; and CRS integrates with Embloom, Bergop, Therapieland, ZorgDomein, ZorgMail and Minddistrict.
items.implication: Several HCI labels appear on a partner's integration list as separate systems, so the promise of the open platform is 'integrate once, reach every label': a versioned partner API with shared credentials, consent and monitoring across FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura and HCI One would cut partners' maintenance and make HCI the default target for new e-health, quality and HIS connectors.

items.title: LDF connection means monthly pseudonymised delivery from the EPD under explicit patient consent, on a platform certified for NEN 7510 and ISO 27001
items.summary: KNGF explains that practices connected to the Landelijke Database Fysiotherapie deliver pseudonymised data from their EPD once per month, that explicit opt-in consent from the patient is required, and that the Keurmerk practice register requires the LDF connection. HCI's home page states that the group is certified for NEN 7510 and ISO 27001.
items.implication: Quality-data delivery is a recurring, consent-gated data pipeline rather than an export button: consent capture at intake, pseudonymisation and monthly delivery monitoring belong in the EPD workflow, the same consent and audit controls serve LDF, Keurmerk and other registers, and the certifications are a selling point only if the consent and audit evidence is visible to practices during insurer and register audits.
